The ingots were prepared in an electrical furnace with pure Mg (99.99%), Mg e30Gd (wt.%), Mg e30Y (wt.%), Mge30Zr (wt.%) master alloys and pure Zn (99.99%) under the protection of mixed SF6 (1 vol %) and CO2 (99 vol %) atmospheres using traditional gravity casting.
The cast ingots were homogenized at 510 /C14 C for 12 h in a resistance furnace.

After homogenization, these ingots were preheated at 410 /C14 C for 30 min and then extruded at a ram speed of 0.5 mm s /C0 1 with an extrusion ratio of 7.11:1. These extrusion rods were quenched into water at ambient temperature.

evidence.quote: The turning point comes to the 6Gd e5Y alloy, which exhibits the best mechanical properties at RT, 250 /C14 C and 300 /C14 C with the UTS values of 359 MPa, 338 MPa and 286 MPa, respectively.

evidence.section: 3.3 Mechanical properties at room and elevated temperatures
evidence.quote: The turning point comes to the 6Gd e5Y alloy, which exhibits the best mechanical properties at RT, 250 /C14 C and 300 /C14 C with the UTS values of 359 MPa, 338 MPa and 286 MPa, respectively.

Firstly, the small sized block-shaped LPSO phase before extrusion provided favorable conditions for the formation of thin plate-shaped LPSO phase at DRXed regions, which effectively hindered the grain boundary migration at high temperature due to superior thermal stability.

Secondly, the profuse lamellar LPSO phases prior to extrusion contributed to the highest density of low angle grain boundaries (LAGBs) and residual dislocations in the extruded 6Gd e5Y alloy, which obstructed dislocation slip at elevated temperatures.
In addition, the abundant lamellar LPSO phase also caused the fine DRXed grain size and strong basal texture to enhance the high-temperature strength of the extruded 6Gd e5Y alloy.
It promotes the nucleation of DRXed grains through particle-stimulated nucleation (PSN) mechanism
According to the Hall-Petch relationship, small size of DRXed grains can effectively prevent dislocation movement through grain boundary strengthening
the thin plate-shaped LPSO and b phases with excellent thermal stability in the DRXed regions could hinder grain boundary migration by increasing the Zener pinning force
This orientation relationship is not suitable for the activation of basal slip, which contributes to high texture strengthening.
the large number of residual dislocations inside unDRXed grains can also improve the mechanical properties by obstructing dislocations both at room and high temperatures
Kink deformation is an important way to coordinate deformation due to the limited slip systems in HCP crystal structure
Especially at high temperatures, the pinning of grain boundaries is extremely critical when a large amount of grain boundary slips exist
